items.title: v0.40.8
items.abstract_or_text: ## Recursive Flint [Flint](https://ollama.com/library/flint) brings Recursive's coding model to Ollama. It is designed for the work coding agents do across a repository: understanding unfamiliar code, tracing bugs, implementing features, and adding tests. Reasoning, multi-turn tool use, and a 262K-token context window support longer tasks across files and tool interactions. Flint is an Apache 2.0-licensed, 40B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with approximately 2.5B parameters active per token. In its [release evaluations](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint#evaluation), Recursive reports 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified. ```sh ollama run flint ``` Note: Flint is supported on MacOS. Other GPU support will be enabled in a subsequent release. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.7...v0.40.8

items.abstract_or_text: llama: create new fused op for QSA mask (#30640) * llama: create new fused op for QSA scoring * enroll glm5.3-next too * tests : initialize the remaining tensors in test_kpool_mask The harness sentinels were left uninitialized, so leftover memory could read as NaN and fail the NaN check. * ggml: generalize the k-pool mask op into ggml_top_k_mask The k-pool mask op only covered the pooled QSA selection of qwen4exp and glm5-next, while the DSA models and the DeepSeek V4 CSA build the same top-k mask by hand with fill, set_rows and add. ggml_top_k_mask(mask, top_k, score, blocks, extra) keeps the mask cells of the live picks and the extra cells, and sets the rest to -inf. Every row tensor is 4D in the layout of top_k, and the mask is broadcast to those rows, so a selection can also be made per head. score, blocks and extra are optional: without score every pick is live, without blocks a pick is a cell, and extra holds the cells a row keeps without a pick. llm_graph_context::build_fused_top_k_mask views the row tensors in the layout of kq_mask and registers the fused node. The k-pool models, the DSA attention of build_attn and the DeepSeek V4 CSA mask use it when the probe enables the op, and keep their current path on backends without it. --------- Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: mtmd : lfm2 tiles and layout match transformers (#30261) * mtmd : lfm2 tiles stretch the image to the grid Lfm2VlImageProcessor.crop_image_to_patches resizes the image straight to (512 * rows, 512 * cols) before it cuts the tiles. llama.cpp kept the aspect ratio and added black bars for LFM2 (only d1-omni stretched), so the tiles of d1-3B and every LFM2-VL / LFM2.5-VL model differed from transformers unless the image had the aspect ratio of the grid. With PAD_NONE the tiles are the same as in transformers. * mtmd : lfm2 layout with Python rounding in double precision Lfm2VlImageProcessor.smart_resize rounds with Python's round (half to even) and computes beta and the tile grid aspect ratio in double. llama.cpp used std::round and float, so 31926 of the 16.7M sizes in [1,4096]^2 got another thumbnail size or grid than transformers (and d1-omni vision.py), e.g. 400x600 -> 416x608 instead of 384x608 and 720x1600 -> 2x5 tiles instead of 2x4. The lfm2 smart resize and grid choice now follow the Python code and match it on every size of that range. * fix --------- Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - It also fixes some other issues listed on the below commits. It contains the following commits: - Fix inputs dict casting in generate (#49731) by @Cyrilvallez - Fix zero expert gradients in bfloat16 with expert parallelism and ep_size < fsdp_size (#49688) by @qgallouedec - Declare the input modalities of the VLMs that report text only (#49677) by @qgallouedec - Avoid a host-to-device copy in eager_mask (#49684) by @hmellor

items.abstract_or_text: server: add realtime transcription API (#30636) * server: add realtime transcription API * drop transcription_sessions * proxy ws * add docs * server: let the API key middleware guard the websocket httplib runs the pre-routing handler before the websocket upgrade, so the API key middleware answers 401 at handshake like any other route. This covers the router proxy, whose children run keyless, and accepts the same key forms as HTTP (Bearer, raw key, X-Api-Key). * server: keep realtime slots out of the prompt loop A realtime slot waiting for audio is GENERATING with nothing to decode, so it fell through the prompt loop and took slot_batched. A request on a higher slot then failed can_batch_with on the task type and starved for the whole session. Realtime slots have no prompt: the loop sets them up once and always leaves them. * server: start the realtime session once its slot is live The audio stream was created in the prompt loop, which skips a slot that cannot batch with the one generating, and session.created went out before the task was posted: early appends failed and the reader quit, leaving the socket open and the slot held until the HTTP timeout. The slot now sets up its stream at launch and signals it with the begin result, session.created waits for it, and a reader that stops closes the socket so the session ends with it. * server: name the committed item in input_audio_buffer.committed Per the Realtime spec, item_id is the item made from the committed audio and previous_item_id the one committed before it, null for the first. committed now comes before the transcript that completes that item, and both go out with the item switch under one lock, so a delta cannot land between them. * server: use the GA transcription session shape The session object follows the GA Realtime schema: type transcription, with the input format, transcription model, turn detection and noise reduction under audio.input. The rate stays the model sample rate, which is what the client must send for now. --------- Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11780/llama-b11780-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) -
